picks.style: sanskrit apocalyptic recitation, tanpura drone and heavy mridangam, deep male voice, ominous, building
picks.why: The portents before Kurukshetra — sun and moon eclipsed in one month, clouds raining blood, a rain of flesh at midnight.

picks.style: gentle sanskrit chant, tanpura and bamboo flute, warm male voice, slow, tender
picks.why: The ascetic standing still as a tree-stump until sparrows nest and lay their eggs in his matted hair.

picks.style: sanskrit funeral lament, sarangi and low drone, keening female-led voices, slow, grieving
picks.why: Kṛpī with unbound hair beside Droṇa's pyre, students heaping it with bows and spears while the Sāman is sung.

picks.style: ancient ecstatic chorus, frame drums and shrill aulos, layered female voices, accelerating, wild
picks.why: The parodos itself: 'The plain flows with milk, it flows with wine, it flows with the nectar of bees.'

picks.style: ritual call and response, deep drums and low horns, antiphonal voices, frenzied, thunderous
picks.why: The palace miracle — 'Shake the world's plain, lady Earthquake!' — already written as call and response.

picks.style: tragic messenger lament, single aulos and low strings, stark solo voice, slow, harrowing
picks.why: Pentheus throwing off the headband so his mother might know him — the most terrible recognition in Greek tragedy.

picks.style: pastoral dirge with refrain, oboe and muted strings, plaintive tenor, slow, mournful
picks.why: Built on repeated 'Teach me' lines and a returning refrain: 'Awake my Pipe; in ev'ry Note express fair Stella's Death.'

picks.style: alternating shepherds' duet, recorder and lute, two light voices trading verses, lilting, courting
picks.why: Amoebean couplets swapped between two singers — cowslip bank, murmuring brook, love kept secret.

picks.style: fairy pastoral, harp and soft flute, clear tenor, gentle, enchanted
picks.why: Ends on the singer whose voice freed the eclipsed moon and brought the fairy queen tripping over the green in blue mantles.

picks.style: english tavern air, fiddle and cittern, hearty baritone, steady, convivial
picks.why: 'To thee, fair Freedom! I retire' — Shenstone's most quoted poem, four square stanzas made for singing at a table.

picks.style: pastoral folk ballad, acoustic guitar and fiddle, warm female vocal, unhurried, bright
picks.why: Trochaic and already tuneful: the milkmaid singing over the brimming pail with cowslips springing around her.

picks.style: comic broadside ballad, banjo-like plucked strings and bodhran, wry male voice, brisk, deadpan
picks.why: A complete joke with a punchline — Richard asks advice, is warned off, marries her, and tells her what Thomas said.

picks.style: greek festival dance, double pipes and clashing cymbals, massed voices with cries, fast, jubilant
picks.why: The closing hymn — Spartan girls like fillies kicking dust beside the Eurotas, hair tossing, feet beating.

picks.style: urgent women's chorus, hand drums and reed pipe, quick female voices, running tempo, breathless
picks.why: The water-carrying chorus racing the fire, with the fountain, the jostling, and the prayer to Tritogeneia.

picks.style: comic antiphonal chorus, plucked lyre and clappers, two opposing groups of voices, brisk, mocking
picks.why: Melanion answered by Timon — two rival tales traded between choruses, built for alternating verses.

picks.style: roman oracular recitation, low drone and single horn, grave male voice, measured, prophetic
picks.why: Only candidate; the Delphic response about the Alban flood and the fall of Veii closes it in real verse.

picks.style: english devotional art song, chamber organ and viol, solemn baritone, slow, valedictory
picks.why: Only candidate, and it is the close of Paradise Lost: 'The world was all before them.'

picks.style: pastoral hymn, solo acoustic guitar, soft tenor, spacious, reverent
picks.why: Only candidate; two famous lines about finding tongues in trees and sermons in stones — short but whole.
